STATE OF VERMONT 
PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION 
 
Case No. 20-0431-TF 
 
Investigation into the tariff filing of Vermont 
Gas Systems, Inc., proposing a change in rates 
and use of System Expansion and Reliability 
Funds 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Order entered:  
 
FINAL ORDER AUTHORIZING NO CHANGE IN RATES AND  
USE OF SYSTEM EXPANSION AND RELIABILITY FUNDS 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
This case involves the Vermont Public Utility Commission’s (“Commission”) 
investigation into the tariff filing of Vermont Gas Systems, Inc. (“Vermont Gas”) requesting an 
overall rate increase of 2.9%, to take effect on a bills-rendered basis on November 1, 2020.  In 
today’s Order, for the reasons discussed below, we approve Vermont Gas’s revised tariff filing 
reflecting a 0% change in base rates and utilization of $5.58 million in System Expansion and 
Reliability Funds (“SERF”).  
II. 
PROCEDURAL HISTORY 
On February 14, 2020, Vermont Gas filed the petition and proposed tariffs reflecting an 
overall 2.9% increase in rates that would be implemented on a bills-rendered basis beginning on 
November 1, 2020.  The proposed overall rate adjustment was comprised of a 3.0% increase in 
base rates, a 2.7% increase in forecasted natural gas costs, and the utilization of approximately 
$5.6 million of the SERF.  The prefiled testimony and exhibits accompanying the original 
petition are as follows: testimony of Ashley Wainer; testimony of Andrea McNeil and exhibits 
VGS-AM-1 through 4; testimony of Todd Lawliss and exhibits VGS-TL-1 and 2; and testimony 
of John St. Hilaire and exhibits VGS-JSH-1, 2, 3.1 through 3.11, and 4.  
On February 28, 2020, the Vermont Department of Public Service (“Department”) 
recommended that the Commission open an investigation to determine whether the proposed 
tariff changes are just and reasonable.

On March 30, 2020, the Commission opened an investigation into the tariff filing.   
On April 9, 2020, the Commission held a scheduling conference.   
On May 22, 2020, Vermont Gas filed a revised cost of service reflecting a 0% change in 
base rates and utilization of $5.58 million of the SERF.  The prefiled testimony and exhibits 
accompanying the revised petition are as follows: supplemental testimony of Ashley Wainer and 
exhibit VGS-AW-1 in pdf and in excel format.   
On June 10, 2020, the Department filed the direct prefiled testimony of Scott Wheeler.  
On July 9, 2020, Vermont Gas filed the second supplemental testimony of Ashley 
Wainer.  
On July 21, 2020, the Department filed the supplemental testimony of Scott Wheeler.   
No party requested an evidentiary hearing in this proceeding.  The Commission received 
no public comments in this case.  After reviewing the record, the Commission has determined 
that an evidentiary hearing is not needed to render a decision in this proceeding.  The testimony 
and exhibits identified above are admitted as if presented at a hearing.1 
III. 
FINDINGS 
1. On February 14, 2020, Vermont Gas filed a Petition seeking approval to implement a 
3% increase to base rates and to return $5.58 million to customers from the System Expansion 
and Reliability Fund (“SERF”).  After that initial filing, the State and federal government 
declared a state of emergency due to the COVID-19 pandemic.  Associated economic disruptions 
have increased unemployment numbers and caused a substantial decline in the 10-year Treasury 
yield.  Wainer supp. pf. at 2. 
2. As part of its effort to support customers through the COVID-19 pandemic, Vermont 
Gas conducted a broad review of its February 2020 cost-of-service filing to determine whether 
adjustments to its proposal for a rate increase could be made to further promote affordability 
while continuing to ensure safe and reliable service through this uncertain period.  Wainer supp. 
pf. at 3.  
 
1 If any party has an objection to any of these documents being entered into evidence, the party shall submit its 
objection within 14 days of the date this Order is entered.

3.  In May 2020, Vermont Gas revised its initial cost-of-service filing to reflect a 0% 
change in base rates, resulting in more affordable natural gas service for its customers.  Wainer 
supp. pf. at 3.  
4. Vermont Gas lowered its cost of service in the revised filing by $1.6 million by 
reducing its return on equity (“ROE”) from 9.2% to 8.65%, reducing the short-term interest rate 
from 2.7% to 1.5%, postponing the in-service date for its Customer Information System from 
Summer 2020 to February 2021, and applying a general cut of $225,000 to operating expenses.  
Wainer supp. pf. at 4-5. 
5. Reducing the proposed ROE to 8.65% is the primary driver of Vermont Gas’s revised 
proposal to hold base rates flat at the current rates.  Wainer supp. pf. at 5. 
6. In its original proposal, Vermont Gas calculated a 9.2% proposed ROE by indexing 
the ROE to 50% of the change in the composite 10-year Treasury note rate, using the three-
month period ending in January 2020.  Wainer supp. pf. at 5. 
7. In its revised proposal, Vermont Gas recalculated its ROE using the three-month 
period ending in May 2020, which resulted in an ROE of 8.65%.  Wainer supp. pf. at 5. 
8. Vermont Gas’s proposal to utilize $5.58 million of the SERF is a key component to 
maintaining a 0% base rate impact on customers.  Vermont Gas anticipates that it will be able to 
utilize remaining funds in the SERF on an annual basis to smooth rates through at least 
September 30, 2023.  Wainer supp. pf. at 8-9. 
9. The use of $5.58 million of the SERF balances the need to mitigate rate impacts at a 
critical time for customers while preserving the ability to stabilize future rate changes with the 
remaining SERF balance over time.  Wheeler pf. at 12.  
10. The proposed, revised cost of service will result in just and reasonable rates.  Wheeler 
pf. at 13.       
IV. 
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS  
Based on the evidence presented in this proceeding, we conclude that a 0% change to 
Vermont Gas’s base rates will result in just and reasonable rates, and that the use of $5.58 
million of the SERF is reasonable and appropriate.  While the Department and Vermont Gas did

Page 4 
 
 
 
not enter into a formal memorandum of understanding or settlement agreement, the Department 
has indicated in testimony that the approach that Vermont Gas took to revising its cost of service 
was reasonable, and the Department supports the base rates and use of SERF funds proposed by 
VGS.  The Department states that it “appreciates Vermont Gas’s commitment to maintain 
existing base rates in response to pressures caused by the [COVID-19] pandemic.”2  The 
Commission also recognizes Vermont Gas’s efforts to hold base rates steady during the uncertain 
economic times that customers are currently facing due to the COVID-19 pandemic.   
The most significant change in Vermont Gas’s proposed cost of service was a reduction 
in its proposed return on equity from 9.2% to 8.65%.  We find this ROE to be reasonable given 
current financial circumstances and given the fact that the Department agrees with the new 
proposed ROE.  We make no determination on whether the use of the change in the value of 10-
year Treasury notes for a three-month measurement period is a generally acceptable method for 
the calculation of ROE under traditional cost-of service-rate regulation.3   
Vermont Gas also proposed to reduce operating expenses by $225,000, though it notes 
that this reduction does not represent a specific, actual savings in operating expenses.  In this 
instance, the revision is a downward adjustment to the cost of service, and the Department has 
agreed that it is reasonable.  If the revision were an upward revision or another party had raised 
concerns about the revision, a greater degree of explanation and documentation would be 
required to verify that the revision was indeed based on known and measurable costs.  The other 
reductions in the cost of service are generally based on a reduction in actual costs and are 
reasonable.   
Vermont Gas’s proposal to use $5.58 million in SERF funds to mitigate rate impacts on 
customers in the coming year while holding adequate SERF funds in reserve to smooth rates in 
future years deviates from the Settlement/Memorandum of Understanding (“8710 MOU”) 
between the Department and Vermont Gas approved by the Commission in Case No. 8710.  In 
 
2 Wheeler pf. at 13. 
3 Regarding Vermont Gas’s ROE calculation, the Department offered the following: “Given the uncertainty 
surrounding the possible impacts of the pandemic, the need for [Vermont Gas] to maintain adequate liquidity, 
[Vermont Gas]’s well-founded intentions with respect to the known and measurable standard, and a shared desire for 
expediency, the Department recommends that the Commission accept [Vermont Gas]’s allowed ROE calculations 
for purposes of rendering an overall decision in the rate case.”  Wheeler, pf. at 8.

Case No. 8710, the Commission approved the 8710 MOU, which included the following 
provision: “Future SERF withdrawals shall be calculated to smooth expected rate increases so 
that the full SERF balance is returned to customers by the end of 2021, resulting in a SERF 
balance of zero by the end of FY2021.”4  In its May 22 supplemental testimony in this 
proceeding, Vermont Gas states, “[W]e continue to anticipate a proposal under which the 
Company will be able to utilize adequate SERF on an annual basis to smooth rates through at 
least September 30, 2023.”5 
Although the 8710 MOU contains standard provisions requiring the Commission to adopt 
the MOU in “all material respects,” it also provides, “The Parties reserve the right in future 
proceedings not referenced herein to advocate positions that differ from those set forth in this 
MOU, except as specific herein and as necessary to implement this MOU.”6  Because both the 
Department and Vermont Gas agree to Vermont Gas’s proposal to utilize $5.58 million in SERF 
funds to mitigate rate impacts on customers in the coming year while holding adequate SERF 
funds in reserve to smooth rates in future years and because the 8710 MOU language 
contemplated future alternative advocacy positions, the Commission does not view approval of 
the proposed SERF utilization as violating the 8710 MOU.  The proposal to use $5.58 million in 
SERF funds to mitigate rate impacts on customers in the coming year while holding adequate 
SERF funds in reserve to smooth rates in future years is reasonable and will help prevent 
dramatic swings in base rates through 2023. 
We have reviewed the documentation in support of the filing, and we conclude that the 
proposal to hold base rates flat and to use $5.58 million in SERF funds will result in just and 
reasonable rates.  Therefore, we approve no change to the base rates and we approve the use of 
$5.58 million in SERF funds.

V. 
ORDER 
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, ADJUDGED, AND DECREED by the Public Utility Commission 
(“Commission”) of the State of Vermont that: 
1. VGS may leave base rates unchanged for the 2021 fiscal year. 
2.   During the rate year, Vermont Gas is authorized to withdraw $5.58 million from the 
System Expansion and Reliability Fund (“SERF”).
